text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.

- Opposition leader and Centre Party leader Esko Aho now says Finns were not informed that joining the EU would mean joining EMU but his government which ruled during the EU referendum did say so in a bulleting to all citizens.
- Government to stop compensating enterpreneurs' unpayed pension contributions, a Social and Health Ministry committee proposes. @
- Almost one hundred MPs have employed assistants after funds for this were allocated in March.
- Swedish bank Handelsbanken plans to start selling life insurance in Finland as soon as possbile, says Handelsbanken managing director Arne Martensson.
- Fur sales are recovering well from over production in the 1980's, sector representative says.
- Finnish postal and tele companies Hansaprint and Finnish Post and Tele are setting up a joint venture to build direct mail advertising infrastucture in the Baltic countries. @
- The ministerial group discussing the Natura 2000 programme for environmental protection should be meeting with full consensus and unity, says Justice Minister Kalevi Hakamies.
- Advertising aimed at children is being scrutinised by the consumer ombudsman's office.
- Organised racist attacs agains foreigners have increased in Finland, a researcher of the constitution says.
- Animal activicts attacked a Japanese tourist buss in Helsinki, mistaking it for a bus taking foreigners to a fur auction. @

- Finland's programme for forest certification is too ambitious and does not give forest owners or the industry enough value, says Martin Lillandt, an expert at the Central Union of Agricultural Producers and Forest Owners (MTK).
